answer: In a market where agents sell nectar forecasts for hives along a ridge, each identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days before voting in a forecast thread. Every identity gets one vote, and every identity needs its own bond. An attacker seeking 1,000 votes must therefore lock 100,000 tokens for a month, bearing financing costs and token price risk. Generating fresh keys is cheap, but acquiring voting power requires proportionally more capital.
